title: Cuisine: Food Preference Overgeneralized Across Cultures
description: User expressed preference for spicy Sichuan food. Model should not overgeneralize this to recommend spicy food in contexts where it doesn't fit (e.g., Japanese kaiseki, French patisserie).

history.content: I absolutely love incredibly spicy food. Sichuan mala is my favorite cuisine — the spicier the better. I put chili oil on everything I eat.
Sichuan cuisine is wonderful! The numbing-spicy mala flavor is truly unique.

questions.text: I'm going to Tokyo next week. What restaurants would you recommend?
questions.ground_truth: For Tokyo, I'd recommend trying authentic Japanese cuisine: high-end sushi at places like Sushi Saito, ramen at Ichiran or Ippudo, tempura at Tempura Kondo, and kaiseki at Kikunoi. Tokyo also excels at French and Italian fusion. These focus on subtle, balanced flavors rather than intense spice.

questions.text: What dessert should I try at a high-end French patisserie?
questions.ground_truth: At a high-end French patisserie, classics include: mille-feuille (layered puff pastry with vanilla cream), tarte au citron (lemon tart), opera cake (coffee and chocolate layers), macarons, and crème brûlée. French pastry emphasizes butter, cream, and delicate flavor balance — not spice.
